WHAT IS DECIMEN OPTICAL TRANSFER?

Decimen Optical Transfer is a proof-of-concept system for transferring files between two devices using a screen, a camera, animated QR codes, and fountain coding.

The sender displays a continuous stream of QR frames while another device uses its camera to capture those frames and reconstruct the transmitted file.

SCREEN → ANIMATED QR FRAMES → CAMERA → RECONSTRUCTED FILE
HOW THE ORIGINAL PROJECT WORKS

The original Decimen Optical Transfer project is built around a one-way screen-to-camera communication channel.

Instead of relying on a normal sequential transfer where a missed frame must be retransmitted, the project uses fountain coding.

The original project uses Luby Transform (LT) coding to create QR frames containing XOR combinations of pseudorandom subsets of the original data blocks.

“Dropped frames cost time, never correctness.”
ORIGINAL PROJECT FEATURES
Screen-to-camera file transfer
Animated QR-code transmission
Fountain-coded transmission
Offline operation after the initial visit
File-name and media-type preservation
Text-snippet transfer
Gzip compression when useful
SHA-256 verification
In-browser playback for received video
Diagnostics and benchmarking tooling

These capabilities belong to the upstream project unless specifically identified below as modifications made in this edition.

MY CHANGES

This edition keeps the original transfer concept and project foundation while introducing a different application-level presentation and user interface.

01 — Unified Application Shell

A single application shell was introduced around the sender and receiver experiences.

02 — Send / Receive / About Navigation

The interface provides dedicated navigation for Send, Receive, and About.

03 — Embedded Send and Receive Views

The modified outer interface separates the Send and Receive views while presenting them through one application shell.

04 — New About Section

A dedicated project-information area was added for attribution, authorship, development information, licensing, and credits.

05 — Dark UI and Visual Integration

The outer interface uses a consistent dark visual system with thin borders, muted text, cyan accents, compact controls, and rounded navigation elements.

06 — Responsive Layout

The outer application interface adapts to smaller displays and mobile screen widths.

PRIVACY & SECURITY

Optical transfer does not automatically mean encrypted transfer.

If the sender is displaying information on a screen, another camera pointed at that screen may potentially observe the transmitted data.

No network path does not mean encryption or confidentiality.

Do not use this project to transmit information that you are not authorized to disclose.

Decimen Optical Transfer GUIDES
TWO-DEVICE TRANSFER GUIDE

Use Send and Receive together

This page explains the reliable way to move a file between two devices. One device displays animated QR codes from Send; the other reads them with its camera from Receive. Open this same HTTPS page on both devices.

01 · START CORRECTLY

Prepare both devices

  1. Host this file on an HTTPS address and open the same link on both devices.
  2. On the sending device, choose Send. On the receiving device, choose Receive.
  3. On the receiver, press Start camera and allow the browser camera permission.
  4. Do not use a local file:// copy on a phone for Receive; mobile browsers can deny its camera access.
02 · SEND A FILE

Sender procedure

  1. Open Send, keep the File mode selected, then choose a file.
  2. Wait for the animated QR display. It repeats continuously while the transfer is active.
  3. Set the sender display to maximum brightness and stop screen dimming or sleep.
  4. Tap the QR display for fullscreen when available. A larger physical code is easier for the camera to read.
03 · RECEIVE A FILE

Receiver procedure

  1. Use the standard rear camera when the phone offers several lenses.
  2. Keep the complete QR code and its white border inside the camera view.
  3. Fill approximately 70–85% of the preview with the QR code, then hold the phone still or prop it on a stand.
  4. Wait for completion. The receiver collects enough frames, reconstructs the file, and checks SHA-256 before offering it.
04 · RELIABLE SETTINGS

Start with these values

  • TX FPS: start at 10–15 fps. Increase only when decoding is consistently smooth.
  • Bytes / Frame: use 1465 first. If the camera cannot decode, reduce to 1000 or 500.
  • Error Correction: use L as the usual starting setting.
  • Display Size: use the largest size that still shows the whole QR and white quiet margin.
05 · POSITION AND LIGHT

Make the QR easy to scan

  • Start close enough that the QR fills most of the receiver preview. For most setups this is about 15–30 cm phone-to-phone or 25–60 cm screen-to-phone.
  • Keep the camera almost parallel with the display. Avoid a steep tilt, glare, shadows, and cutting off any edge of the QR.
  • Use even room lighting, keep the sending screen bright, and avoid direct reflections from lamps or sunlight.
  • Clean the camera lens and let autofocus settle. Movement and refocusing reduce the number of useful frames.
06 · IF NOTHING HAPPENS

Troubleshoot in order

  1. Confirm both devices are using this same version of the page and that the second device is on Receive.
  2. Confirm the camera permission and an HTTPS address on the receiver.
  3. Lower Bytes / Frame to 1000 or 500, then set TX FPS to 10.
  4. Increase brightness, enlarge the QR, choose the correct rear camera, and stabilize the phone.
07 · IMPORTANT LIMITS

Factors outside the program

Camera focus speed, lens quality, sensor noise, browser camera support, display brightness, reflections, refresh behavior, and room lighting differ between devices. The program cannot override those physical limits. The optical stream is also not encrypted: any camera that can see the QR may read it, so do not send sensitive material in an untrusted place.
